rows.name: PitchBook
rows.investor_coverage: Investor totals conflict and none could be checked on a primary page (403): 634K+ on PitchBook's investor page (search snippet, vendor claim, undated); 667K+ in an unverified snippet attributed to a PitchBook page; third-party figures of 597K (Claude Academy), 570K (ZoomInfo), 450K+ as of Sept 2026 (InvestorLists.vc, a competitor) and 423K+ (Apify).
rows.sourcing_notes: Methodology page could not be fetched (403). A job listing says the core product depends on analysts who 'collect, verify, structure, and enrich private market data' (Seattle Senior Analyst, July 2025, $150K–$200K); notes group PitchBook with vendors using LP/GP surveys and calls. Headcount ~1.8K (Revelio, Sept 2025); 1,748 observed profiles in July 2026, ~36% in Seattle, 'Research Associate' top title at 8.3% (Unify GTM); no data-researcher headcount disclosed. Kaplan & Lerner (2016) note PitchBook and Preqin are the only major sources identifying GPs by fund name.
rows.verification_notes: Analyst verification per job listing; no published record-level accuracy metrics, researcher headcount or survey response rate.
rows.known_issues: Investor totals conflict across sources (423K–667K). G2: 'outdated information on niche companies' (36 reviews) and 'financial information and deal tags often do not match reality' (20), e.g. PE ownership still listed years after a sale. TrustRadius: 21% of reviewers raise timeliness of updates.
rows.pricing: Quote-only. Vendr median ~$30,000/yr, range $20K–$124K, ~14% average negotiated savings; additional seats ~$7K/yr; 1-year minimum, no monthly billing; tiers reportedly renamed Core, Pro and Pro Plus in March 2026 (CostBench, verified 11 Oct 2026; notes the Vendr source no longer loads). Other estimates: $12K–$20K per seat (VCBeast); Vendr list estimate $20K–$40K+ per seat (Prova).
rows.licence_terms: Use limited to 'Licensee's internal business operations'; Raw Data may go into work product only if it 'has no material independent commercial value'; no downloading or exporting substantial portions as raw data on a standalone basis; no use to develop a competing product. Export caps such as 1,000 rows/day seen in a UK government order form; academic licences prohibit data mining.
rows.weak_spots: Stale data on niche companies, ownership and deal tags; no published investor-type or regional breakdown; methodology and researcher headcount undisclosed; licence forbids reuse and competitive use.

rows.name: Preqin
rows.segment: private markets LP and fund data
rows.investor_coverage: 16,638 PE investors ('confirmed, active allocators') on the PE product page fetched Oct 2026 (vendor claim); 4,592 family offices for 2023 from Preqin's 2024 report as cited by competitor Altss (third party, not confirmed on Preqin's site); 210,000 private-market funds at the Mar 2025 BlackRock close (vendor claim).
rows.sourcing_notes: 'One-to-one conversations form the backbone' of data collection, plus 'thousands of sources every day' (regulatory filings, press releases, news, websites); relationships with managers and investors since 2003; FOIA requests to public pensions. In-house team of 450+ multilingual analysts (undated UMass page). Performance data primarily from public pension filings, FOIA and voluntary GP (~60%) and LP submissions (Kaplan & Lerner, pre-2024). Investor profiles: future PE plans, active fund searches and mandates, full commitment history, decision-maker contacts. Acquired by BlackRock 3 Mar 2025 (~£2.5bn cash); standalone product being integrated into Aladdin and eFront.
rows.verification_notes: Cross-checks data during validation and clarifies data points directly with the firms concerned; says it will 'never just use machines'. No published accuracy metrics.
rows.known_issues: Kaplan & Lerner (2016, pre-2024): misses top funds without public-pension LPs (e.g. Sequoia, Accel); stale data because responses are tardy; reports IRRs without cash flows; performance data for ~70% of committed capital in the 2000s. Family-office count not confirmed on Preqin's own site.
rows.pricing: No list price. Vendr median $49,334 (low $27,674, high $77,221) per Investables; $15K–$75K+/yr depending on asset classes per Multiples.vc.
rows.weak_spots: AUM and dry powder listed for fund managers, not investors; counts exclude inactive investors and those active only in other asset classes; voluntary reporting makes performance data stale; misses funds without public-pension LPs.

rows.name: Crunchbase
rows.investor_coverage: ~300K investors (institutional and individual) among ~4M entities (~40% US) and 700K+ funding rounds 1990–2024, from the OECD's June 2025 extract (independent); Crunchbase's own data page gives no entity counts.
rows.sourcing_notes: Five inputs: 'market experts' (venture partners and contributors), user-engagement signals from 80M+ users, proprietary ingestion systems, 1,000+ news outlets and government filings, and analyst validation. Venture Program: 4,000+ members send monthly portfolio updates in exchange for data access; 600K+ contributors update 100K+ profiles a month (help page ~1.5 years old); 30M+ 'verified updates' a year. In 2017: 3,000+ firms and ~500K contributors (OECD 2017, pre-2024).
rows.verification_notes: Claims 'AI grading algorithms' plus human validation, continuous benchmarking against external sources and a global analyst team; contact data carries ML confidence scores. Claims 84% of funding events 'anticipated', but its 16K+ vs 14K+ 'correctly predicted events' figures are inconsistent on the same page and no method is disclosed. Retterath & Braun (2020, pre-2024) rank it among the best-covered, most accurate databases and best value for price.
rows.known_issues: G2 cons: 'Missing Information' (17 reviews), 'Outdated Information' (15); contact-data accuracy 7.7/10 across 140 reviews; disclaims liability for contact accuracy. OECD: investor-type tags not harmonised, government VC and CVC arms not identified; startups registered at an average age of ~3 years; incomplete coverage before its 2007 launch causes survivorship bias. Over-represents IT, software, biotech and healthcare (Retterath & Braun 2020, pre-2024).
rows.pricing: Pro $49/user/mo billed annually (~$588/yr) or $99 monthly; Business ~$199/user/mo; 10 free contacts a month, then paid packs ($29 for 100 up to $99 for 500); exports ~2,000 rows/mo on Pro and 5,000/mo on Business (Sept 2026). Enterprise/API: no published price; Vendr-reported median ~$20,000/yr across 71 purchases, range $4,440–$51,377. Free API tier reported gone in 2026. Self-serve is the only published list price in the market.
rows.licence_terms: Terms and robots.txt prohibit scraping; resale requires authorisation (secondary sources; full ToS not retrieved). Export caps ~2,000 rows/mo (Pro) and 5,000/mo (Business); API limited to 200 requests/min per key.
rows.weak_spots: US-centred (~40% of entities US; uniquely covers >40% of North American entities); good for list-building but weak for qualifying investors (profiles show investment counts and portfolio, not ticket size or AUM); lumps angel groups, family offices and individuals together in category mappings.

rows.name: Dealroom
rows.investor_coverage: 250K+ investors in 900K+ transactions 1990–2024 per the OECD June 2025 extract (independent); Dealroom's FAQ (Aug 2026) gives 3.2M+ companies, 1.5M+ startups and 500K+ European startups but no investor count (vendor claim).
rows.sourcing_notes: Five streams: official filings and trade registers; 100+ government and ecosystem partners supplying local data; founder and investor submissions (manually checked); public web (news, job boards, websites); predictive models. OECD adds domain registries, web and app-store analytics, investor portfolios and third-party data, and finds Dealroom more likely to capture early-stage deals (angel, spinouts, crowdfunding). Profiles cover VC firms, PE funds, corporate investors, angels and LPs.
rows.verification_notes: 'AI-powered data collection verified by humans'; partners help catch errors and corrections are reviewed before publishing; verification by its 'Intelligence Unit'. No published accuracy metrics.
rows.known_issues: OECD: investor-type tags not harmonised, government VC and CVC arms not identified; startups registered at an average age of ~3 years; coverage before its 2013 launch incomplete (survivorship bias). Partner count inconsistent across its own pages (100+, 'over 90 governments', 'over 75').
rows.pricing: Premium ~€12,500–12,600/yr with a 3-seat minimum, up to ~€41,000 for 20 seats; Premium Plus ~€17,000/yr (Peony, corpdev.ai). Business emails credit-metered (3,000 credits on Premium Plus). Billed annually; API is a separate plan; MCP server for AI agents; free public no-auth endpoints exist.
rows.licence_terms: Bulk export and API require paid plans; licence terms not published in the FAQ and not retrieved directly.
rows.weak_spots: Europe-centred (only ~30% entity overlap with Crunchbase; each uniquely covers ~35% of European entities); publishes no investor counts; lumps angel groups, family offices and individuals together in category mappings.

rows.name: CB Insights
rows.investor_coverage: No investor-profile count published; 13M+ company profiles (vendor claim, undated); Smart Money 2025 covered 12,000+ venture investors with 10+ unique portfolio companies over 2015–2025, a lower bound on its active-VC universe (vendor claim). OECD calls its US coverage broadly similar to Crunchbase's.
rows.verification_notes: Marketed as 'Double verified'; no method published.
rows.pricing: ~$40K–$60K for 1–3 seats, median ~$47K (corpdev.ai); $46,984 verified purchase median (CostBench); $40K–$100K per team (Multiples.vc).
rows.licence_terms: 90-day cancellation notice in standard terms (per InvestorLists.vc).
rows.weak_spots: Investor universe size not disclosed; verification method undisclosed.

rows.name: Tracxn
rows.investor_coverage: 71,500+ investor profiles and 3.7M+ entities in a Nov 2024 investor deck filed with BSE (vendor claim); 72,900+ per Screener.in (third party relaying company data); university guides cite 200,000+ (third party, conflicts with company figures). OECD calls its US coverage broadly similar to Crunchbase's.
rows.known_issues: Investor counts conflict (71.5K–72.9K in company figures vs 200,000+ in Stanford and IIT Roorkee guides); personal emails provided only 'in many cases'.
rows.pricing: Free 'Lite' tier; ~$550/mo individual (SaaSworthy, via Multiples.vc) or ~$500/mo (InvestorLists.vc); team licences $6,500–$15,000/yr (Multiples.vc).
rows.weak_spots: Investor universe size unclear across sources; partial personal-email coverage.

rows.name: S&P Capital IQ Pro + With Intelligence
rows.segment: LP/GP intelligence in a financial data platform
rows.investor_coverage: With Intelligence brings ~30,000 investors (PE, private credit, infrastructure, hedge funds, family offices) and ~30,000 managers, per deal materials relayed by Crowdfund Insider (third party, undated); S&P closed the acquisition 25 Nov 2025. OECD calls Capital IQ's US coverage broadly similar to Crunchbase's.
rows.sourcing_notes: With Intelligence data is 'sourced directly from LPs/investment allocators and GPs/fund managers'. Since June 2026 Capital IQ Pro's private-markets data comes from With Intelligence; the platform also carries Cambridge Associates benchmarks (2.5K+ managers, 9.5K+ funds). Before that, a 2024 S&P–Preqin partnership supplied 60K+ firms and 196K+ funds. S&P paid $1.8bn; With Intelligence had ~3,000 customers and ~$130M expected 2025 revenue.
rows.pricing: No published price for Capital IQ Pro; quote or demo only.

rows.name: LSEG Workspace / VentureXpert
rows.segment: PE/VC deal and fund data in a financial terminal
rows.investor_coverage: 46,000+ PE/VC firms, 96,000+ funds and 217,000+ PE/VC-backed companies on one LSEG page vs 43,000+ firms, 91,000+ funds and 316,000+ companies on another (vendor claims, undated); Investment Professionals dataset: 241,000 professionals at 46,000 firms in 70 countries.
rows.sourcing_notes: Formerly Refinitiv/Thomson Reuters; sourcing method not described in the notes.
rows.known_issues: Two LSEG pages give conflicting counts. Stucke (2011, pre-2024) challenged VentureXpert's reliability for PE/VC performance; Thomson Reuters rejected the critique. Kaplan & Lerner (2016, pre-2024): large inconsistencies with VentureSource and quality deterioration; reports <10% of investments as defunct when >20% are, though it has ~40% more rounds and ~10% more post-money valuations across 449 common firms. Kaplan, Sensoy & Strömberg (2002): VentureSource had almost twice as many valuations, with average absolute error 60% of VentureXpert's. Maats et al. (2011): low consistency with VentureSource; VentureXpert more reliable for fund-level work.
rows.pricing: No published price; quote or demo only.
rows.weak_spots: Foreign-market coverage only 'select' (US well covered); failed investments under-reported.

rows.name: PEI Group (Private Equity International)
rows.investor_coverage: No investor or LP count given; 70,000+ funds, 12,000+ actively raising and 11,000+ with performance data (vendor claim, undated).
rows.sourcing_notes: Direct manager and investor submissions, regulatory filings (SEC, FCA and equivalents) and PEI editorial research; notes group PEI with vendors using LP/GP surveys and calls.
rows.verification_notes: 'Every record is reviewed and validated by PEI's research team'; unverifiable data is 'flagged or excluded rather than published'.
rows.pricing: No published price; quote or demo only.
rows.weak_spots: Publishes no investor or LP count.

rows.name: Mergermarket
rows.investor_coverage: No investor count found; '400,000+ deals' since 1998 per a comparison site (third party, not confirmed by ION).
rows.pricing: No published price; quote or demo only.

rows.name: FINTRX
rows.investor_coverage: 4,600 family offices worldwide in Q2 2026 (+96 that quarter; from a search summary, PDF not machine-readable) and 4,503 as of 31 Mar 2026 (vendor claims); Apr 2024: 1,870+ single- and 2,130+ multi-family offices with 23,000+ contacts; also 46,000+ RIA/broker-dealer firms and 802,000+ registered reps.
rows.sourcing_notes: A '75+ person research team' tracks family-office direct investments (Apr 2024). Most newly added multi-family offices are non-SEC-registered international firms. Profiles include AUM and asset-class preferences (Apr 2024: typical AUM $100M–$400M; PE 78%, direct investments 71%, real estate 60%).
rows.pricing: No published price; quote or demo only.

rows.name: Wealth-X (Altrata)
rows.investor_coverage: Product page gives no counts of dossiers or family offices (sister products BoardEx: 1.8M executives, 2.2M organisations; RelSci: 10M+ profiles; vendor claims).
rows.sourcing_notes: Dossiers 'built, verified and updated by a team of 400+ researchers'.
rows.verification_notes: Details 'substantiated by two independent, credible sources'.
rows.pricing: No published price; quote or demo only.

rows.name: Signal by NFX
rows.investor_coverage: No official current total found; 18,830+ investors per Beancount directory (third party, undated); launched Feb 2017 with 4,500 investors, mostly Silicon Valley and Israel (pre-2024); 349 lists across 103 sectors and 4 stages per an unaffiliated scraper.
rows.sourcing_notes: Investors add themselves to up to 10 lists via their 'Investment categories', or a trusted community member adds them. Ranking draws on self-reported data, founder activity, Gmail-derived connectedness and community upvotes. Profiles show deal histories and connections.
rows.verification_notes: NFX says profiles are for investors 'highly sought after by Founders and vetted by them and by other investors'.
rows.known_issues: Self-listing sits awkwardly with the 'vetted' description, so the list should not be treated as a census.
rows.pricing: Free to founders (implied by the platform model; no price page reviewed); premium-feature pricing not found.
rows.weak_spots: Self-selected coverage, originally concentrated in Silicon Valley and Israel; no official total published.

rows.name: OpenVC
rows.investor_coverage: Counts vary by source: 20,000+ 'verified investors' as advertised, 16,000+ and 5,000+ elsewhere (third-party reports, undated; which figure comes from which of the three sources is not recorded); OpenVC's own pages returned 403.
rows.sourcing_notes: Self-claimed investor profiles; fields include check size, lead preference, geography and industry.
rows.known_issues: Investor counts inconsistent across sources (20K+, 16K+, 5K+); check-size fields largely self-reported.
rows.pricing: Pricing page could not be fetched (403).
rows.weak_spots: Self-reported qualification fields; official total not found.

rows.name: Unicorn Nest
rows.investor_coverage: Homepage claims 37,602 investors (VC, CVC, family offices, angel syndicates), 33,253 partners and 226K VC deals collected since 2019, with no type split (vendor claim, undated); released 26,000 VC funds as a free spreadsheet in Apr 2020 (pre-2024).
rows.sourcing_notes: Data collected since 2019; method not described. Country pages include PL, CZ, EE, LV, LT, HU, RO, SK, SI, BG and UA.
rows.pricing: Homepage advertises a 'FREE Investor Database'; current paid pricing not found. In 2020 it charged $5 per AI-match query (pre-2024).
rows.licence_terms: The 2020 free dataset was licensed under terms barring academic and commercial use (pre-2024).
rows.weak_spots: No investor-type split; CEE country pages but no CEE-specific count.

rows.name: Vestbee
rows.investor_coverage: VC list focused on CEE, the Baltics and Europe with filters for ticket (€0–5M+), stage (pre-seed to buyout/PE) and ~99 sectors; no total count shown and access requires login (vendor page).
rows.sourcing_notes: Check-size fields largely self-reported. Co-publishes CEE ecosystem reports with Dealroom.
rows.weak_spots: No published count; login required; check sizes largely self-reported.

rows.name: Landscape.vc
rows.segment: startup discovery and deal sourcing (not an investor database)
rows.investor_coverage: Publishes no investor counts; a startup-discovery tool rather than an investor database (page dated 21 Aug 2026).
rows.sourcing_notes: Monitors '15+ alternative data sources' (GitHub trending, Product Hunt, YC launches); refreshes daily.
rows.pricing: $30 for a 30-day trial; per-seat monthly pricing in 3 tiers, no annual commitment (page dated 21 Aug 2026).

rows.name: Harmonic
rows.segment: startup and company discovery for deal sourcing
rows.investor_coverage: No investor count published; 35M+ companies and 195M+ people (vendor claim, undated).
rows.sourcing_notes: Proprietary web data plus 'routine portfolio updates from the world's leading investors'.
rows.pricing: ~$10K–$30K/yr (API-scoped estimate, Multiples.vc).

rows.name: Grata / Sourcescrub
rows.segment: private company discovery and deal sourcing
rows.investor_coverage: No investor count; Sourcescrub covers 16–17M companies from 220–290K sources (third party, undated).
rows.sourcing_notes: Websites, job postings, news, regulatory filings, trade-publication mentions, conference attendee lists and speaker rosters, and industry award lists. Grata acquired by Datasite in June 2025 (reported $200M+); Sourcescrub sold to Datasite in Aug 2025 and being merged into Grata.
rows.pricing: Grata: $15K–$40K/yr; a Vendr-based 25-seat range of $28K–$155K (CostBench).

rows.name: Inven
rows.segment: private company discovery and deal sourcing
rows.investor_coverage: No investor count; 28M+ companies, 100M+ entities, 430M+ contacts and 3M+ transactions (vendor figures relayed by corpdev.ai, undated).
rows.sourcing_notes: Says data is collected and maintained in-house, not licensed from PitchBook, Capital IQ or FactSet. Raised a $12.75M Series A in May 2026.

rows.name: Beauhurst
rows.investor_coverage: Claims coverage of every private company in the UK and Germany (vendor claim); no investor count found.
rows.sourcing_notes: Primary source is SH01 share-allotment filings at Companies House, treated as more reliable than press releases. The ONS, which uses Beauhurst data in national accounts, confirms it captures all filed UK unlisted-equity issuances from 2015; 2011–14 covered only announced deals; only cash-for-shares issuances are counted.
rows.verification_notes: Independent ONS use and confirmation of UK filing coverage from 2015.
rows.known_issues: Internally inconsistent on unannounced rounds: 70% of UK investment activity (blog) vs ~50% (comparison page).
rows.pricing: No published price; quote or demo only.
rows.weak_spots: 2011–14 data covers only announced deals; non-cash share issuances excluded; investor count not published.

rows.name: AngelList
rows.investor_coverage: No current public count of angels or syndicates found; only 2015 platform statistics (pre-2024). OECD calls its US coverage broadly similar to Crunchbase's.

rows.name: Altss
rows.investor_coverage: 9,000+ single family offices (vendor claim, undated); about 2x the best-documented counts and treated in the notes as unverified marketing.
rows.known_issues: 9K+ SFO claim is unverified and roughly double the best-documented counts (FINTRX ~4.6K in 2026; Preqin ~4.6K for 2023).
rows.pricing: From $12,000/yr for family-office coverage (PrivateEquityList comparison).

rows.name: Venture Capital Archive
rows.investor_coverage: 40,000+ family offices and LPs combined (vendor claim, undated).

rows.name: InveXora Family Office DB
rows.investor_coverage: 36,000+ 'verified' contacts (vendor claim, undated).

rows.name: Angel Match
rows.investor_coverage: 125,000+ angels and VCs and 99,000+ 'verified' emails (vendor claims reported by InvestorLists.vc, a competitor; undated).
rows.verification_notes: Claims 'verified' emails but publishes no verification methodology (as of Sept 2026).
rows.pricing: $59–$349/mo with export caps of 100–1,200 rows/mo (InvestorLists.vc).

rows.name: InvestorHunt
rows.investor_coverage: 110,000+ investors (vendor claim reported by InvestorLists.vc, a competitor; undated).
rows.verification_notes: Claims 'verified' emails but publishes no verification methodology (as of Sept 2026).
rows.pricing: $57–$297/mo (InvestorLists.vc).
